intro: Art directors make creative decisions, coordinate teams and manage deadlines, skills that media and marketing leadership value. The closest of the 25 careers below is Producers and Directors, with an 81% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $90,360, which is 21% less than the $114,850 art directors earn.
why_it_works: Leading a creative team means setting the visual direction, giving clear feedback and keeping designers, writers and clients aligned. O*NET rates judgment at 3.75 out of 5 for this job, and complex problem solving, coordination and time management at 3.62. Production, game design and advertising use the same skills. All matches need no new degree. The gaps are reading people and technical operations.
tips: Advertising and Promotions Managers earn $133,660, which is 16% more, and are a 73% match.
Marketing Managers earn $166,790, or 45% more, and value strong creative leadership.
Video game design is a 76% match with a median of $104,000 for its broader group.

faq.q: What jobs can former art directors do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Producers and Directors (81%), Video Game Designers (76%) and Advertising and Promotions Managers (73%), based on O*NET 31.0. Writers and Authors are 71% matched but earn $76,910, which is 33% less than the $114,850 art director median.

faq.q: Which careers for art directors pay more?
faq.a: 7 of the 25 matches pay more. Computer and Information Systems Managers earn $175,140 (52% more), Marketing Managers $166,790 (45% more) and Sales Managers $148,270 (29% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. These roles reward experience leading teams and budgets.

faq.q: Do art directors need another degree?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than art directors already have, including all of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 57% of workers in the closest match, so your portfolio and leadership record count most.

faq.q: What skills should art directors build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are social perceptiveness, operation and control, troubleshooting and operations monitoring. Coordination already rates 3.62 out of 5 for art directors in O*NET, so reading clients and managing operations are the main steps toward marketing leadership.
